answer_1.quote: We focus on the commonly utilized functions for content creation, i.e., polishing, continuation, abbreviation, expansion, (automatic) creation, formatting, and correction... We divide the on-device LLM features released by representative smartphone manufacturers into 5 categories, encompassing a total of 20 tasks.
answer_1.outputs: Summaries of documents, calls, recordings, meetings; answers to text Q&A (document, retrieval, personal); refined or generated text for content creation tasks (polishing, continuation, abbreviation, expansion, creation, formatting, instant reply, correction); extracted entities/relations/events; notification sorting and message summarization results.

answer_3.quote: Evaluations of subjective tasks are commonly conducted using the LLM-as-a-Judge paradigm. In SmartBench, we develop detailed automated evaluation criteria for each category/task and use GPT-4 Turbo (and also Qwen-Max) as the judge LLM.

answer_4.quote: We carry out a human test with six human experts... we ask human experts to rank the outputs generated by different on‑device models for each question.
answer_4.guideline: Human experts rank model outputs per question; rankings are compared to LLM‑as‑a‑Judge scores using Pearson correlation.
